main_body: Two-storey timber-frame and stone house. A large hipped tile roof sits over a half-timbered upper wall and a cobblestone ground floor with a door, windows and a hanging sign.
top_band: At x=48 the roof is orange and red tile rows, light L~130-144 alternating with dark L~58 lines, from rows 4 to about 43. A dark eave row at rows 44-45 closes it.
evidence: The tall hipped roof reads as a large sloped top surface: the side hips are foreshortened, the ridge sits at the top, and the tiles are lit on the upper edges. It is clearly separated from the vertical walls by a dark eave shadow band at rows 44-45. Below it, the grey cornice line at about row 74 marks the floor edge. The windows have sills and flower boxes, the door is set into the stone, and the sign projects from the wall. The structure matches the Beodeul reference houses, with roof as top surface and walls as front face.

style.evidence: The candidate has 19 median colours per tile against 18 and 11 for the references. Flat-fill coverage is 0% and it has 191 distinct colours. The roof tiles carry per-tile highlights, the plaster is speckled, and the cobbles are shaded one by one. Dark edge pixels are only 12% neutral, so the outlines lean brown or plum and follow the adjacent material. It would sit next to the references without looking thinner.
